mainTopic: Who can build a חזקה, why a גזלן's proof fails, and whether a sale made under force is valid
overview: The amud opens by finishing an answer. A woman whose divorce is in doubt can still build a חזקה in her husband's property, even though, following רבי זירא, he still has to feed her. Then רב נחמן quotes רב הונא: the people who cannot build a חזקה can still win with real proof, but a גזלן's proof is not accepted. The גמרא asks why this is needed, since a משנה about buying from a סיקריקון already voids such a purchase. The answer is that רב הונא rejects רב, who said a שטר makes the purchase valid. רב הונא follows שמואל instead: even a שטר does not help unless it includes אחריות נכסים. רב ביבי adds, in the name of רב נחמן, that the גזלן loses the land but gets his money back, though only if witnesses saw him pay, not if they just heard the owner admit it out of fear. Finally, רב הונא rules that a sale made by someone hung up until he agreed is valid. The גמרא rejects one reason for this and begins to quote a ברייתא as the real source, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The wife rule applies in a 'divorced and not divorced' case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its answer. The earlier ruling that a divorced woman can build a חזקה in her husband's property was needed for a woman whose divorce is in doubt. Following רבי זירא, her husband still has to feed her, so we might have thought she could not build a חזקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case is a woman who is 'divorced and not divorced.' This follows רבי זירא, who said in the name of רבי ירמיה בר אבא in the name of שמואל: wherever the חכמים said a woman is 'divorced and not divorced,' her husband must still pay for her food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes an answer that began before this section. The ruling that a divorced woman can build a חזקה is needed for a woman whose divorce is uncertain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא's rule says the husband still owes a half-divorced woman מזונות. So you might have thought he would not bother to protest if she used his land, which would mean her use proves nothing. The ruling teaches that she can still build a חזקה in his property.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman whose divorce is in doubt; she is both 'divorced and not divorced'
Food and support a husband must provide his wife
Obligated
Wherever the חכמים said; it introduces a rule that applies across many cases

steps.whatToRemember: Even when a divorce is in doubt and the husband still owes her food, she can build a חזקה in his property.

phrases.english: In a case where she is divorced and not divorced,
and this follows Rabbi Zeira,
as Rabbi Zeira said
that Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba said
that Shmuel said:
Wherever the Sages said:
'divorced and not divorced,'
her husband is obligated in her food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer to the earlier question of why the ruling that a divorced woman can build a חזקה was needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Places the rule in a specific case (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzMaskana: The ruling that a divorced woman can build a חזקה is needed for a woman whose divorce is in doubt. Even though her husband still owes her מזונות, she can build one.

steps.title: Real proof works for everyone except a robber
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן quotes רב הונא. All the people who cannot build a חזקה win if they bring real proof, but a גזלן's proof is not accepted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: הונא told me that all of them, if they bring proof, their proof is proof, and the court leaves the field in their hands. A robber who brings proof, his proof is not proof, and the court does not leave the field in his hands.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins. The people who cannot build a חזקה just by using a field can still win with real proof, but a גזלן cannot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's list (partners, sharecroppers, guardians, husband and wife, and so on) only lose the power of חזקה through use. They can still win with a שטר or witnesses. A גזלן is different, because we worry that his proof was squeezed out by force, so even his proof is not trusted.

keyTerms.meaning: Proof, such as a document or witnesses
A robber; someone who takes property by force
The court leaves (or places) the field in his possession

steps.confusionAlert: 'All of them' does not mean all people in general. It refers to the people listed in the משנה who cannot build a חזקה, such as partners and family members.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that losing the power of חזקה is not the same as losing your rights. Only a גזלן's proof is suspect.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן, אָמַר לִי הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said: Huna told me:
All of them who brought proof,
phrases.notes: 'All of them' means the people in the משנה who can't build a חזקה.

phrases.english: their proof is proof,
and we place the field in their hands.
A robber who brought proof,
his proof is not proof,
and we do not place the field in his hands.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן, אָמַר לִי הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the list of people who cannot build a חזקה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: People who cannot build a חזקה still win with real proof, but a גזלן's proof is not accepted.

steps.title: Why say this? A משנה already teaches it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רב הונא adds. A משנה already rules that if someone buys from a סיקריקון and then buys again from the original owner, the purchase is void.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is this teaching us? We already learned: if someone bought land from a סיקריקון and then went back and bought it from the owner, his purchase is void!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב הונא's teaching as unnecessary. It cites a משנה that seems to say the same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, a violent man forced the owner off his land. The owner's later 'sale' to the buyer does not count, because he only sold under pressure. That already shows that a deal tied to robbery is not trusted, so רב הונא's rule seems to add nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: What is this teaching us? It challenges a teaching as unnecessary
We already learned it in a משנה
A violent person who took land from its owner by threats
His purchase is void

phrases.english: What is this teaching us?
We already learned:
If one bought from a Sikarikon,
and then went back and bought from the owner,
his purchase is void!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב הונא's rule in step 2 as already taught.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's rule that a גזלן's proof is not accepted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סיקריקון משנה already voids a purchase that comes after a robbery, so the new rule seems unnecessary.

steps.title: רב הונא rejects רב's view about a שטר
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא's rule comes to reject רב. רב said the סיקריקון purchase is void only if the deal was done by word of mouth, but with a שטר the buyer acquires the land.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to exclude the view of רב, for רב said: they taught this only when the owner told him, 'Go, take possession and acquire.' But with a document, he acquires.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The משנה alone could be read narrowly the way רב reads it, and רב הונא is coming to reject that reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב limits the משנה: a sale made only by word of mouth is void, but a sale backed by a written שטר is valid. רב הונא says a גזלן's proof is not proof, so a plain שטר does not help in a robbery situation. That is something new beyond the משנה, and the next step explains exactly how far it goes.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude; to reject a different opinion
They taught this only in the case of
Go take possession and acquire, a verbal-only transfer
A written legal document

steps.confusionAlert: רב does not disagree that a deal with a סיקריקון is a problem. He only says a written שטר is strong enough to make the sale work.

phrases.english: To exclude the view of Rav,
for Rav said:
They taught this only where he said to him:
phrases.notes: 'They taught this' means the סיקריקון משנה from the step before.

phrases.english: 'Go, take possession and acquire,'
but with a document, he acquires;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 3 by showing what רב הונא adds.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The teaching comes to reject another opinion (לאפוקי)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Following רב, a purchase backed by a שטר would be valid even after a סיקריקון.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב הונא teaches that even a שטר does not help, because a גזלן's proof is not proof.

steps.title: רב הונא holds like שמואל: even a שטר is not enough without a guarantee
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא completes its answer. רב הונא teaches the view of שמואל: even with a שטר the buyer does not acquire, unless a property guarantee is written.
steps.simpleTranslation: He teaches us that the law follows שמואל, who said: even with a document the buyer does not acquire, until the seller writes a guarantee on the property.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining why רב הונא's rule is needed. It teaches that the law follows שמואל, not רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said a שטר is enough to make the סיקריקון purchase work. שמואל says a שטר alone is not enough. Only a שטר with אחריות נכסים shows the owner truly meant to sell. רב הונא's rule, that a גזלן's proof is not accepted, matches שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: "He teaches us". This shows the new point a statement adds.
A property guarantee. The seller promises to pay the buyer back if a creditor takes the land.
A written document, here a bill of sale.

steps.whyThisMatters: Now we see why רב הונא's rule is not extra. Without it, we might have followed רב and accepted a plain שטר.

phrases.english: He teaches us that it is like שמואל –

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר: אַף בִּשְׁטָר נָמֵי לֹא קָנָה,
phrases.english: who said: even with a document, he does not acquire,
phrases.notes: "He" is the buyer who bought from the סיקריקון.

phrases.english: until he writes a property guarantee.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer from Step 4 by naming whose view רב הונא follows.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the statement adds a new point: it decides the argument between רב and שמואל.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since a משנה already exists, we might have thought רב הונא adds nothing, or that a שטר helps, as רב says.
steps.terutzMaskana: A שטר does not help unless it has אחריות נכסים, like שמואל.

steps.title: The גזלן loses the land but gets his money back
steps.stepSummary: רב ביבי adds, in the name of רב נחמן: the גזלן has no claim to the land, but he does get back the money he paid.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ביבי finishes the teaching in the name of רב נחמן: he has no land, but he does have money.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ביבי adds an ending to רב הונא's rule about the גזלן. The גזלן does not keep the land, but the owner must return the money he received.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא said the גזלן's proof does not win him the field. That leaves an open question about the money he paid. רב נחמן's answer is that the sale is cancelled, but the payment is not lost.

keyTerms.meaning: "Concludes it". He adds an ending to an earlier statement.
Land.
Money.

phrases.english: And רב ביבי concludes it
phrases.notes: "It" means רב הונא's rule from Step 2, that a גזלן's proof is not accepted.

phrases.english: in the name of רב נחמן:

phrases.aramaic: קַרְקַע אֵין לוֹ, אֲבָל מָעוֹת יֵשׁ לוֹ.
phrases.english: He has no land, but he does have money.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב בִּיבִי מְסַיֵּים בַּהּ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רב הונא's rule from Step 2 and adds what happens to the money.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The גזלן loses the field, but the owner must give him back his money.

steps.title: He gets his money back only if witnesses saw the payment
steps.stepSummary: The money is returned only when witnesses saw the גזלן count out the money. If they only heard the owner admit he was paid, there is no refund, because the owner may have admitted out of fear.
steps.simpleTranslation: When is this said? When the witnesses said, "He counted out the money to him in front of us." But if the witnesses said, "He admitted to him in front of us," then no. This is like רב כהנא, who said: if he had not admitted it, the גזלן would have taken him and his donkey to the taskmaster.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא limits when the גזלן gets his money back. He gets it only when the witnesses actually saw the money handed over.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the witnesses only heard the owner say "I was paid," that proves nothing. The owner may have said it because he was afraid of the גזלן. רב כהנא explains that if the owner had refused to admit it, the גזלן would have turned him and his donkey over to a cruel official.

keyTerms.meaning: "In what case is this said?" This opens a limit on a rule.
He counted out the money to him.
He admitted to him that he was paid.
A taskmaster, a cruel official.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up "he counted out" (מנה) with "he admitted" (הודה). Only seeing the money counted out proves a payment. An admission made under fear proves nothing.

phrases.english: In what case is this said –
where witnesses said: "In front of us he counted out the money to him,"

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אָמְרוּ עֵדִים: ״בְּפָנֵינוּ הוֹדָה לוֹ״ – לֹא;
phrases.english: but if witnesses said: "In front of us he admitted to him" – no;
phrases.notes: Here the owner admitted to the גזלן that he had been paid.

phrases.english: like רב כהנא, who said:
if he had not admitted to him,

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה מַמְטֵי לֵיהּ לְדִידֵיהּ וְלַחֲמָרֵיהּ לְשַׁחְווֹר.
phrases.english: he would have brought him and his donkey to the taskmaster.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the refund rule from Step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The refund applies only when witnesses saw the money paid, not when they only heard an admission that could have come from fear.
steps.whatToRemember: A גזלן never keeps the land. He gets his money back only if witnesses saw him pay it.

steps.title: A sale made by someone hung up until he agreed is still valid
steps.stepSummary: A new teaching from רב הונא: if people hung someone up and he then sold, his sale is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: if they hung him up and he sold, his sale is a sale.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic connected to sales made under pressure. רב הונא rules that even a sale forced by hanging someone up still counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sounds surprising, since the seller clearly did not want to sell. The גמרא will now search for the reason behind this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: They hung him up, for example from a tree.
His sale is a valid sale.

phrases.english: רב הונא said:
If they hung him up and he sold – his sale is a sale.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic tied to the earlier talk about sales made under pressure.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sale made under physical force is valid.

steps.title: Suggested reason: every seller is under some pressure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason and suggests one: people sell only because they need to, and their sales still count. So a forced sale should count too.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? Whatever a person sells, if he were not pressured he would not sell, and even so his sale is a sale.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רב הונא's rule is true. It suggests a proof from ordinary sales.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Almost nobody sells his property unless some need pushes him to. We still treat those sales as fully valid. So pressure alone should not cancel a sale, and this should be true even when the pressure is being hung up.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
Forced, under pressure.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Whatever a person sells,

phrases.aramaic: אִי לָאו דַּאֲנִיס – לָא הֲוָה מְזַבֵּין,
phrases.english: if he were not pressured – he would not sell,
phrases.notes: The pressure here is his own need for money.

phrases.english: and even so, his sale is a sale.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks for the reason behind רב הונא's rule in Step 8.
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's rule that a forced sale is valid.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Logic: every ordinary sale is made out of need, and those sales are valid.

steps.title: Pressure from your own needs is different from force by others
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. Pressure from your own needs may be different from force that other people put on you.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe pressure that comes from yourself is different from pressure that comes from others!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back against the reason it just suggested.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person who sells because he needs money still chooses to sell. Someone hung up by others is being forced by them. Because the two cases may be different, ordinary sales cannot prove that a forced sale counts.

keyTerms.meaning: "But maybe". This often opens a rejection.
Pressure that comes from one's own needs.
Force put on a person by others.

phrases.english: But maybe pressure from himself is different
from pressure from others!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִילְמָא שָׁאנֵי אוּנְסָא דְנַפְשֵׁיהּ מֵאוּנְסָא דְאַחֲרִינֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof offered in Step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the suggested reason. רב הונא's rule itself still stands.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof treats self-made pressure and force from others as the same, but they may be different.

steps.title: The real source is a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sets up a different source for רב הונא's rule: a ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is like what was taught in a ברייתא:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא drops the rejected reason and gets ready to quote a ברייתא as the real source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "אלא" tells us the earlier reason is set aside. The ברייתא itself comes next. It will show that force from others still allows a valid act.

keyTerms.meaning: "Rather". It drops the previous idea.
"As was taught" in a ברייתא.

phrases.english: Rather, as was taught in a ברייתא:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the reason rejected in Step 10 with a new source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב הונא's rule is based on a ברייתא, which will be quoted next.
